subject: Acme — Rate limits & overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme — Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Nice to meet you and the Acme team. Quick recap and next steps so we all stay aligned:  

Summary from our discovery call:
- Workload: conversational AI for product search, chat assistants, and lightweight summarization across web/mobile.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~50M tokens/day (we heard ~1.5B tokens/month as a baseline).
- Burst profile: marketing events & product launches could spike traffic 6–10x baseline for short windows (minutes–hours).
- Target unit economics: your finance team is looking for target pricing in the ~$20–$35 per 1M tokens range; you mentioned ~$25/1M as an initial target.
- Budget: you indicated a monthly target budget of $40k–$75k to start (ramp expected).

Open questions / asks from us:  
1) Can you share a 30-day traffic profile (tokens/day or requests/sec histogram) so we can model batching/caching benefits?  
2) Do you prefer hosted (pay-as-you-go with overage caps) vs. dedicated/reserved capacity (committed $ with lower unit price)?
3) What SLOs matter most: 95th latency, p99, or strictly sub-200ms tail for inference?

What I’ll do next: Rafael will scope potential overage terms and burst handling, Camila will propose an initial rate-limit/quota configuration and estimate how much caching will reduce token counts, and I’ll put together a draft mutual action plan and preliminary pricing sheet. I’ll share a first-pass pricing/MAA doc by Fri (attached in follow-up).

If the above looks right, can you confirm the token baseline (50M/day) and the target $/1M token we should model ($25/1M)? That will let us produce a concrete AS-IS vs committed pricing comparison.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0143

Subject: Re: Acme — Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the recap, this is helpful. Confirming a few items from our side:  

- Baseline: the 50M tokens/day estimate is correct for our current MVP traffic. If the pilot succeeds we expect growth to ~120M tokens/day over a 3–6 month period.
- Burst behavior: during product announcements and email campaigns we have historically seen traffic spikes up to ~8x baseline for short bursts (10–90 minutes). For budgeting we assume four marketing spikes per month.
- Budget & target unit economics: our leadership indicated a starting budget target of $50k/month with flexibility if unit economics are favorable. Our procurement target for benchmarking is $25/1M tokens or lower for committed capacity; we’re open to $30/1M on hosted with reasonable overage caps.

Answers to your Qs:  
1) I’ll export and send a 30-day token histogram by EOD Wed (sending to you + Camila).
2) We’re leaning committed/dedicated if the committed price meets the target $/1M, otherwise hosted with predictable overage is acceptable for the pilot.
3) Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms is acceptable for now; p99 < 800ms preferred.

Appreciate you pulling together a draft MAA; once we have your numbers we’ll route internally to procurement.

Best,
Alex
Senior Product Manager — Acme Corp
alex.taylor@acmecorp.com

Thanks Alex — that helps a lot. Quick notes while we model:  

- For committed pricing, we’ll produce a 3-tier committed model (quarterly commit) that hits the $25/1M target at the mid-tier and improves with larger commits. That will include burst allowances and a smoothing policy so short spikes don’t immediately trigger overage.
- For hosted pricing, we’ll show a pay-as-you-go unit price and an overage policy. Typical overage guidance we model internally is a premium of 1.25–1.75x the base hosted unit price depending on burst duration and whether the customer wants guaranteed burst capacity. We’ll be explicit about burst-window definitions (e.g., sustained >5x baseline for >30m).

Can you confirm whether the spikes you described are typically single-region (US) or multi-region? Multi-region burst behavior affects capacity reservation recommendations. Also if you can send the 30-day histogram that will let Camila estimate cache hit rates and effective token reduction.

I’ll aim to get the first-pass MAA + pricing sheet to you by Fri EOD. Rafael — looping you to own the pricing scenarios and overage language. Camila — can you start with a rate-limit/quota proposal based on a 50M/day baseline and 8x burst headroom?

—
Marissa

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up (technical details)

Alex / Marissa — quick technical notes that will feed the pricing model and MAA:  

Rate limits & burst handling (proposal):
- Baseline config: token/sec rate limit sized for 50M tokens/day ≈ 578 tokens/sec sustained (24/7 smoothing). We model request-level batching that effectively raises throughput while reducing per-token overhead.
- Burst allowance: allow token/sec bursts up to 8x baseline for short windows using a token-bucket style burst buffer (config: burst multiplier = 8, bucket refill tuned to baseline).
- Sustained burst policy: if average over a 30-minute sliding window exceeds 5x baseline, classify as sustained and subject to quota enforcement/overage. Short spikes (<30 min) will be absorbed by burst buffer and not billed as overage.
- Quota increases: self-serve quota increase requests for hosted customers usually handled within 24–72 hours for moderate increases; for committed/dedicated we recommend a planned capacity bump (48–72 hour notice to warm dedicated pools).

Caching & effective token reduction:
- With prefix/KV caching for product search responses we conservatively estimate 10–25% effective token reduction for Acme’s access patterns; for very repetitive prompts this can exceed 40%. That will materially change the effective $/1M tokens.

Overage pricing considerations (what Rafael will model):
- Short bursts (absorbed by buffer): no overage.
- Sustained over-threshold usage (>30m at >5x): overage billed at premium (proposed 1.5x base hosted unit price) unless covered by committed capacity.
- Emergency guaranteed-burst add-on: for customers who need guaranteed headroom, we offer a burst reservation add-on charged as a % of committed capacity.

I’ll attach a short technical appendix with the quota policy and recommended default rate-limit values for your 50M baseline.

—
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
